text: N230775March 19, 2014CLA-2-62:OT:RR:NC:N3:356CATEGORY:	ClassificationTARIFF NO.: 6205.20.2026Mr. John M. PetersonMs. Elyssa EmsellemNeville Peterson LLPCounselors at Law17 State Street- 19th FloorNew York, New York  10004 RE:	The tariff classification of a men’s dress shirt from China.   Dear Mr. Peterson and Ms. Emsellem:In your letter dated August 13, 2012, you requested a tariff classification ruling, on behalf of your client, Best Key Textiles Limited.  The response was delayed due to laboratory analysis.  As requested, your sample will be returned.Style BKY 006 is a men’s shirt constructed from woven fabric.  You state that the fiber content is 45% polyester, 55% cotton woven fabric.  Style BKY 006 features a self-fabric collar with collarband; a left-over-right, full front opening with seven button closures; long, vented sleeves with button closures on the cuff; a rear yoke; and a curved, hemmed bottom. The garment will be imported in blue and white stripes.  The garment has no metallic character or appearance.In your ruling request, you recommended classification of the submitted garment in subheading 6205.90.40 Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS), which provides for men’s or boys’ shirts of other textile materials or 6205.20.20 which provides for men’s or boys’ shirts of cotton.You further rest your claim on New York Ruling Letter (NYRL) N187601, dated October 25, 2011, which classified a yarn with similar metal content, made in the same process, in heading 5605, HTSUS, as a metalized yarn.  We note that NYRL N187601 was revoked by Headquarters Ruling HQ H202560, dated September 13, 2013, which classified the yarn in question in subheading 5402.47.90, which provides for synthetic filament yarn (other than sewing thread), not put up for retail sale, of polyesters.  Furthermore, we sent this sample to the U.S. Customs and Border Protection laboratory to determine the fiber content.  The laboratory has determined that the sample is constructed of a one 1-ply cotton/polyester blend yarn in the warp and in the weft.  The lab analysis also indicates the presence of trace aluminum and some other metals, which is in agreement with the findings you submitted from a private lab. Based on the lab analysis, the fact that the garment has no metallic character or appearance, and in accordance with the reasoning set forth in HQ H202560, we find that the one 1-ply yarns are not metalized yarns of heading 5605, HTSUS, but have a fiber content of 53.1% cotton, 46.9% polyester.The applicable subheading for Style BKY 006 will be 6205.20.2026, HTSUS, which provides for men’s or boys’ shirts: of cotton: other: dress shirts: other: men’s.  The duty rate is 19.7% ad valoremDuty rates are provided for your convenience and are subject to change.  The text of the most recent HTSUS and the accompanying duty rates are provided on the World Wide Web at http://www.usitc.gov/tata/hts/.This ruling is being issued under the provisions of Part 177 of the Customs Regulations (19 C.F.R. 177).A copy of the ruling or the control number indicated above should be provided with the entry documents filed at the time this merchandise is imported.  If you have any questions regarding the ruling, contact National Import Specialist Rosemarie Hayward at (646) 733-3064.Sincerely,Gwenn Klein KirschnerActing DirectorNational Commodity Specialist Division
